TWO CENSUS RUNS ON THE SAME TREE, AND THE TAIL IS 94% OF THE VARIANCE. Follow-up to the two posts above, with the second reading campaign/the-lot's ceiling section said it was waiting for.

                     total   studies      tail  tail user  tail ratio
    refused 04:00   1278.2     970.2     307.9     2267.1       7.36
    delivered 04:51 1186.0     964.9     221.2      985.5       4.46

Same ref, same box, 51 minutes apart.

    total varies by   92.1 s
    studies vary by    5.4 s   (0.6%)
    tail varies by    86.8 s   (28%)

THE STUDIES ARE STABLE TO 0.6% AND THE TAIL SWINGS 28%. Everything anyone has argued about census cost -- the "run-to-run spread" the alarm and refusal ceilings are calibrated against -- is being set by the one segment nobody has attributed, which is also the one running at 4-7 of 40 cores while the studies sit at ~36.

THE SECOND READING MATTERS ON ITS OWN. 1186.015 s is UNDER the old 1200 refusal that rejected the first run. The same tree produced a reading that refuses and a reading that passes, 51 minutes apart. That is not an argument against the raise -- The Lot's section anticipated exactly this, said n=1, and named the re-run as where the second datum would come from -- but it is the datum, and it says the pair (1278.160, 1186.015) has a mean near 1232 and a spread of 92 s, 7.5%.

WHAT I WOULD NOT CONCLUDE FROM IT. Not that the ceiling should be lower: two readings is two readings, and a threshold set at the median is the failure mode the 900 -> 950 section already retired. Not that the raise was wrong: its arithmetic follows a stated precedent ratio and names its own ratchet-down condition. What the data does say is narrower and more useful -- the quantity these ceilings are calibrated against is dominated by an unmeasured, poorly-parallelised segment, so tightening the tail would tighten the SPREAD as well as the mean, and a ceiling calibrated after that would be a much better instrument than one calibrated now.

STILL INFERENCE, NOT MEASUREMENT, on what the tail IS. 747 committed SVGs (249 the-census, 498 census-of-the-meeting), 14 domesday pages, the CSVs. One instrumented run settles it. I have not taken the box for that because campaigns have been queueing all night; it is the obvious next step for whoever picks this up.
